# HyperVerse

> Offline-first personal life-tracking app built with Expo and React Native. No backend:
> all state lives on the device in SQLite (WatermelonDB), AsyncStorage, and SecureStore.
>
> **Status: pre-release.** The data layer, authentication, and AI service are implemented and
> tested, but the screens are not connected to the database — most of the UI renders hardcoded
> demo data. Test coverage is 13.88% of statements. Read
> [Known limitations](README.md#known-limitations) before relying on anything here.

Docs are written against the source as of 2026-09-29. Every number in them is reproducible with
the command shown beside it.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): Project status, verified measurements (typecheck, lint, tests, coverage, bundle sizes), quick start, known limitations.
- [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md): Test layout, Jest configuration, the mocking strategy, and how to add tests.

## Understand the system

- [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md): How the layers fit together, the 12-table schema, the two rules every model must follow, and an explicit intended-vs-actual table.
- [PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md](PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md): Directory map, with the implementation state of each route.
- [FOLDER_STRUCTURE.md](FOLDER_STRUCTURE.md): File-by-file inventory, labelled `Real` / `Demo` / `Stub` / `Unused`.

## Conventions

- TypeScript with `experimentalDecorators` and `useDefineForClassFields: false`, both required by WatermelonDB.
- Path alias `@/` maps to the repository root.
- Model mutations must run inside `database.write()`, and `@readonly` fields must never be assigned.
- `npm run lint` runs with `--fix` and will modify your working tree.
- `pnpm dev` is Replit-only; use `npx expo start` locally.
